tokenizer.name: cl100k_base
tokenizer.implementation: lumen_core::tokenizer::count_tokens, the function the meter uses
tokenizer.caveat: cl100k_base is not Claude's tokenizer. Counts compare modes with one another; they are not a bill and not the number of tokens Claude would charge.
tokenizer.counted: the reply text of a tool call. The JSON-RPC envelope and `_meta` are not counted, exactly as the meter does not count them.
tokenizer.line_endings: files are read byte for byte from the git object database; no line-ending conversion happens anywhere

latency.clock: std::time::Instant, a monotonic clock, nanosecond resolution
latency.warmup_note: per series per pass, run the same way as the recorded runs, so caches, page tables and the ledger file are warm; hook spawns are warm-start, not first launch after boot
latency.percentile_method: nearest-rank: the percentile p of n runs is the run at rank ceil(p x n / 100) of the sorted runs, fastest first, with no interpolation. With n = 200 the median is run 100 (of the two middle runs of an even count, the faster), p90 is run 180, and p99 is run 198, which leaves the slowest 2 runs above it.
latency.samples_note: not written. Each series carries `pass_medians_ns`, the median of each pass on its own, in pass order: how far they sit from one another is how much the machine moved while the run was going on.

model.rates_note: rates.rs labels these Sonnet 3.5 / 3.7 / 4 pricing. The harness does not check them against a current price list; they are the model's inputs, not a quote.
model.inputs_source: measured_defaults: means over 19,161 main-agent turns of the Lumen author's own sessions (econ.rs); another user's profile differs
model.formula: value of one saved token = (cache_write + cache_read x rounds_remaining) / 1e6 dollars; one intercepted Read costs one extra round = (context x cache_read + output x output_rate) / 1e6 dollars; a dollar figure below is the median saved tokens of a call x the value of one token
